## Natural history notes

A medium-sized rhinoceros beetle characterized by a shiny dark brown to black oval body, strong digging legs, and a roughened head and thorax. In Florida, the Sugarcane Beetle is found in fields, lawns, pastures, gardens, agricultural areas, roadsides, and other open habitats with grasses, crops, or moist soil. Adults may come to lights and can feed on roots, stems, or underground plant parts, sometimes damaging sugarcane, corn, turf, and other grasses, while the larvae live in soil and feed on roots and decaying organic material.
